module_name: Ethics, Law, and Governance in Social Media Analytics
module_description: Module 28 is the ethics spine of the course: IRB/ethics review, data protection (UU PDP No. 27/2022, GDPR), the public-is-not-permissible principle for social data, anonymization and re-identification risk, algorithmic accountability and platform transparency, bias and fairness in models, and responsible publication (code/data sharing, replication). Students produce an ethics/data-management note for their own capstone.
core_concepts: Ethics frameworks for computational social research
Personal data protection law (UU PDP, GDPR) applied to platform data
IRB/ethics review workflow for student research
Algorithmic accountability and bias in analytics models
learning_outcomes: C3 Apply legal and ethical criteria to an analytics plan
C4 Write an ethics/DPIA note for a capstone project
C5 Evaluate bias and fairness implications of an analytics model
methods_models: Risk assessment (DPIA-style), bias auditing of model outputs, anonymization evaluation (re-identification tests)
Policy analysis using platform documents as corpus
evaluation_metrics: Rubric-graded ethics memo; optional re-identification success rate as empirical check
pitfalls_limitations: Treating public data as automatically usable, weak pseudonymization (usernames are identifiers), group-level harm from model errors, publishing identifiable graphs
tools_stack: DPIA templates, anonymization/evaluation scripts, policy corpus tools
lab_activities: Draft and defend an ethics / DPIA note for a proposed capstone dataset; peer-reviewed against the course rubric
datasets_apis: Policy documents, platform transparency reports and Terms of Service as a text corpus; no personal data collected
assessment_methods: Ethics/DPIA note graded with a rubric; includes defence of sampling, retention, anonymisation and disclosure choices
data_collection_workflow: Identify data and legal basis -> DPIA/risk assessment -> collect only what is needed -> anonymise -> document retention and disclosure -> preserve the ethics note
textbooks: Zafarani et al., Social Media Mining, ethics chapter
AAAI/ACM ethics guidance for computational research
key_papers: 2024-2026 papers on data protection and platform research; AI-use disclosure guidance for research
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: AI-use disclosure became a journal requirement, and platform data protection enforcement tightened, so analytics teaching must integrate compliance documentation
industry_relevance: Ethics and governance are now screening criteria in research assistantships, editorial fact-checking units and trust-and-safety hiring; the module produces an IRB-ready data-management note that is directly reusable in capstone projects.
localization_context: UU PDP No. 27/2022 obligations (legal basis, minimization, retention), Indonesian academic norms on student research ethics (kaji etik), and local debates on election data research are the worked examples.
ethics_regulation: The module itself: data protection principles, consent and re-identification risk, IRB/ethics-review workflow, research reproducibility duties, algorithmic accountability (DSA/platform transparency), and consequences of violating platform Terms of Service.
case_study_scenarios: Produce the ethics/DPIA note for your capstone and defend its sampling and retention choices.
